experiments.what: Preparation. Baseline hashes recorded (eval/stage6/baseline_hashes.json). Held-out set drafted with the Stage 5 sampling procedure (seed 20261009, eval/stage6/sample_holdout.py), approved by the project owner without changes (H-N9 and H-C6 kept despite split answers; the two sampled overlaps kept), frozen as eval/stage6/holdout_questions.json and marked read-only. No retrieval system has been run on it.

Tie-break for equal RRF scores in code-aware hybrid. baseline = BM25 rank wins (Stage 4); T1 = vector rank wins; T2 = neutral (better of the two ranks, then chunk order). Implemented in src/retrieval_v2.py; src/vectorstore.py unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: Letting vector rank decide ties promotes module descriptions above programme tables without losing any Top-5 hits.
experiments.fixed: index, chunks, embedding model, RRF k=60, 50 candidates per retriever, routing, vector-only route for questions without codes
experiments.data: Stage 5 development set (30 scored questions); baseline variant reproduced Stage 5 routed top-10 exactly for all 35 questions; no new chunks needed grading
experiments.latency: no additional computation (same candidate lists, different sort key)
experiments.recommendation: T1: provisional accept (meets +2 Top-1 rule: 15 -> 18, no Top-5 change), to be confirmed after S6-2 as the no-reranker fallback. T2: reject (14 Top-1; in practice breaks ties by page order, which favours tables).
experiments.caveat: Development evidence only. The tie-break was diagnosed on these same questions, and only 7 of 20 code questions have a rank-1 tie, so the effect rests on 7 cases.

decision.T1: provisionally accepted as the Stage 6 configuration and the no-reranker fallback; final decision after S6-2
decision.limitation: T1 is not the final fix for table-versus-description ranking: on C9 it prefers a description where the question needs a programme table

experiments.what: Cross-encoder reranking of T1 routed candidates (src/rerank.py). Models: BAAI/bge-reranker-base (rev 2cfc18c9, file hash verified) and cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2. Pools N = 5, 10, 20, 30; ranks after the pool keep T1 order up to rank 10. Reranker sees chunk text without the citation header.
experiments.hypothesis: A cross-encoder separates description-wanting from table-wanting questions and neighbouring clauses; a pool above 10 also recovers C10.
experiments.fixed: index, chunks, embedding model, routing, T1 candidate generation, RRF settings
experiments.grading: 42 chunks first seen in S6-2 graded blind (eval/stage6/grades.json, 4 graded 2); Stage 5 grades unchanged
experiments.latency_caveat: Single timed pass per configuration; medians do not rise consistently with pool size, so the machine's background load is mixed in. A repeated, interleaved re-measurement (eval/stage6/bench_s6_2_latency.py) was stopped by Claude Code because the system was low on memory (2.7 of 15.9 GB free) and has not been re-run.
experiments.recommendation: Reject bge-reranker-base (lower quality than MiniLM, hurts N1/N2/N9, over the latency budget at every pool size). Accept MiniLM. The pre-agreed pool rule selects N=5; N=10 additionally fixes C10 (+1 Top-1/Top-3/Top-5) for about +150 ms median, and choosing it would be an owner override of the rule.

decision.reranker: cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 accepted; BAAI/bge-reranker-base rejected (lower quality, larger model, higher load cost and latency)
decision.pool: N=10 - DOCUMENTED OWNER OVERRIDE of the pre-agreed smallest-pool rule, which selected N=5. N=10 did not win under the original rule.
decision.override_reason: MiniLM@10 vs @5: Top-1 23->24, Top-3 27->28, Top-5 28->29, MRR@10 0.845->0.875, C10 rank 10->1; extra median reranking latency small and within the experimental budget
decision.provisional_configuration: T1 candidate generation -> top 10 candidates -> MiniLM cross-encoder rerank -> best 5
decision.fallback: T1 (no reranker) when reranking is unavailable
known_limitations: N7 regressed rank 3 -> 4 (out of Top-3, still in Top-5); natural-language Top-3 9 -> 8
C9 (needs a programme table) still rank 2: MiniLM does not fix this table-versus-description case
E3 ambiguous code still rank 2 (Stage 7 requirement)
N4 still a Top-10 miss (target of S6-3)
latency from a single noisy pass; repeated re-measurement stopped for low system memory and not yet re-run

experiments.what: Heading-aware retrieval: same chunks/ids/text; inherited document headings (src/structure.py v2) added to the embedded text and BM25 tokens only; new index faiss_store_v2/ (corpus fingerprint identical to faiss_store/). A: MiniLM sees original chunk text. B: MiniLM sees heading + chunk text.
experiments.hypothesis: Inherited headings let retrieval find chunks whose own text lacks the question's words (target N4), without harming other questions.
experiments.compared_against: accepted configuration: T1 -> top 10 -> MiniLM -> best 5 on faiss_store/
experiments.fixed: chunks, chunk text, embedding model, routing/code filter (body only), T1 tie-break, pool 10, MiniLM

heading_detection.note: v1 defects found by the seed-63 sample were fixed in v2 before any index build; v2 measured on a fresh sample; file eval/stage6/s6_3_heading_check.md

disclosures: The 'heading at the top of a chunk governs it' bug was noticed on chunk 38 (the N4 answer chunk); the fix is a general rule.

Stage 5 analysis wrongly said N4's heading was in another chunk; chunk 38 starts with its own heading. The gain comes from the inherited part title (MIDLANDS STATE UNIVERSITY ACT) plus the heading in the indexed text.

n4_diagnosis.v2_heading: Section: MIDLANDS STATE UNIVERSITY ACT > 5 Membership of the University

B: C5 (needs a programme table) rank 1 -> 4: the SEMA102 description chunks now carry the heading 'SEMA 102 Linear Mathematics', and the table chunk carries a wrong inherited heading (SEGE 405 ...)

experiments.observation_not_preregistered: T1 on faiss_store_v2 without any reranker scores 23/29/30 (MRR 0.875) vs T1 on faiss_store 18/28/28, close to B (24/28/30, MRR 0.883).
experiments.recommendation: Reject A (meets neither criterion; MiniLM without headings pushes N4 from retrieval rank 1 to 8). Provisionally accept B under criterion B (N4 miss -> rank 1, Top-5 29 -> 30, no question leaves the top 5, no category loses more than 1 at Top-3, Top-1 unchanged), recording the C5 and N1 regressions. Development evidence only.

decision.A: rejected: heading-aware retrieval moved N4's answer chunk to candidate rank 1, but MiniLM without the heading pushed it back to rank 8
decision.B: provisionally accepted under Criterion B: N4 miss -> rank 1; overall Top-5 29 -> 30; no question leaves the top 5; overall Top-1 unchanged (24)
known_regressions: C5 (needs a programme table) rank 1 -> 4; an incorrect inherited heading on the table chunk (SEGE 405 ...) contributed
code_in_context Top-3 10 -> 9 (C5); natural_language Top-3 8 -> 9; overall Top-3 unchanged at 28
B added rerank latency P95 2.76 s (single noisy pass), close to the 3 s budget
decision.limitation: heading detection v2 is 24/30 correct on a fresh sample; heading extraction is an imperfect component
rules: Do not tune the heading detector further using the Stage 5 development questions
decision.S6-4: not triggered under the predefined rule (code questions 17/20 Top-1 >= 16; no description-answer code question misses the top 5); skipped for now
S6-6_additions: Add arm: T1 on faiss_store_v2 without MiniLM (development 23/29/30)
To fix before S6-6: B is the primary candidate for the held-out claim; a pre-stated rule for the reranker-free arm; whether to include the isolated S6-1 tie-break arm
decision.fallback: still T1 on faiss_store/; whether it moves to faiss_store_v2 to be decided after S6-6
decision.heading_review: owner reviewed 10 random v2 cases (seed 65): 8 correct, 2 wrong; agrees with all 10 of Claude's verdicts

heading_detector_frozen.rule: no further detector changes, from the Stage 5 questions or from this review
known_limitations: chunk boundaries: a chunk starting with the end of one subsection gets the next subsection's heading (overlap)
table notes and values read as numbered headings (e.g. '6 Compulsory modules plus 2 electives', '3 Years (Visiting)')
faculty names in front-matter lists read as part titles
module code and title on separate lines not recognised (e.g. BMS 116)
a 'sub' heading (Level/Semester) found later in a chunk is combined with the section governing its start
some programme titles truncated when the wrapped line is not joined
a programme table can inherit the previous programme's module heading (seen on C5's table chunk)

experiments.what: Ambiguous course codes: a code -> titles map built from the yearbook text (src/ambiguity.py); codes with more than one distinct title are flagged and reported with their pages. Metadata only: retrieval and ranking unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: Codes like SEMA204 can be detected from the corpus so Stage 7 can name every meaning instead of picking one.

development.E3: SEMA204 flagged; both meanings ('Real Analysis' p.556, 'Introduction to Numerical Methods' pp.571/573) are in variant B's top 5
development.C10: BM135 flagged; 'Commercial Law' (14 places) and 'Business Law I' (Sci p.432 programme table) - checked, genuine in the corpus

precision.v1_seed66: about 10/20 genuine (same-module title variants counted as ambiguous)
precision.v2_seed68: 16/20 genuine (fresh sample after the title-matching fix)

experiments.title_matching_change: v1 -> v2 after the seed-66 sample: compare titles by shared words (>=75% of the shorter title, any order), drop bracketed notes and titles that are lists of other codes; measured again on a fresh sample (seed 68). Not tuned on Stage 5 questions.
experiments.recommendation: Accept as metadata for Stage 7; no ranking change.

decision.S6-5: accepted as metadata for Stage 7; retrieval and ranking unchanged
known_limitations: ambiguity-flag precision 16/20 on the sampled cases

experiments.what: Held-out evaluation of four arms on the frozen held-out set (opened once, 2026-10-08 02:54:12); frozen system at commit 88293e9 (eval/stage6/s6_6_freeze.json)
experiments.grading: 137 blind grades (129 top-5 pool + 8 ranks 6-10); owner spot-check 20/20; judgement calls H-N7, H-N3 p.132, H-N8 p.716, H-E3 p.537, H-C6 approved

primary_claim.wording: Passing means the system passed the predefined Stage 6 engineering/generalisation criteria; it is not statistical proof of generalisation (30 in-scope questions).

reranker_value.rule: if within one at both, discuss explicitly whether MiniLM justifies its complexity and latency (recommend dropping it as simpler and cheaper); otherwise recommend keeping it

decision.conclusion: Arm 3 passed our predefined Stage 6 engineering and generalisation criteria on the frozen held-out evaluation. This is evidence from the 30-question in-scope held-out benchmark and must not be described as statistical proof of generalisation.

final_configuration.main: T1 tie-break -> heading-aware index (faiss_store_v2/) -> top 10 candidates -> MiniLM reranker (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) using heading + original chunk text -> best 5 evidence chunks
final_configuration.fallback: T1 tie-break -> original index (faiss_store/) without MiniLM reranking

decision.minilm: kept: on the held-out set Arm 2 (no MiniLM) achieved 21/30 Top-1 and 26/30 Top-5 vs Arm 3 25/30 and 28/30, so the reranker provides meaningful held-out benefit
limitations: H-N1: sufficient evidence appears only at rank 7
H-C6: cannot be answered sufficiently from a single current chunk; the required evidence is split across chunks
H-C5: remains a ranking weakness for structured/table information
Heading detection is approximately 80% accurate; incorrect inherited headings can affect ranking
The evaluation contains only 30 in-scope questions
Out-of-scope handling, ambiguity behaviour and generated answer quality were not evaluated by S6-6
The held-out set is now seen and must not be reused as an unseen benchmark after future retrieval changes
rules: Do not tune the retrieval system based on these held-out results

arms.3: T1, faiss_store_v2/ -> top 10 -> MiniLM (heading + text) -> best 5 (primary)

s6_6_approval.rules: as proposed 2026-10-08 (freeze before opening; one run of all arms; blind pooled 0/1/2 grading; owner spot-check of 20 grades before metrics; primary claim Arm 3 vs Arm 0: Top-5 not lower, Top-1 +3, more improved than worse, latency within budget; reranker-value rule; tie-break rule; fallback rule)
s6_6_approval.wording: Passing means the system passed the predefined Stage 6 engineering/generalisation criteria; not statistical proof (30 in-scope questions).
s6_6_approval.reranker_rule_note: If Arm 2 is within one question of Arm 3 at both Top-1 and Top-5, explicitly discuss whether MiniLM justifies its complexity and latency.
s6_6_approval.after_opening: held-out set becomes seen data; no retrieval changes based on it may be reported as unseen performance
